author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island’s September 11–13 calendar spans stand-up comedy, theater and two very different music gatherings, giving residents several options across Providence, South Kingstown and Woonsocket.

Comedian Tom Papa is scheduled to perform at The Vets in Providence at 8 p.m. Friday. Trinity Repertory Company is also continuing its run of “The Getaway Driver,” a production built around a true-crime story and playing through October 4.

On Sunday, the first South County Folk Festival is set for noon to 9 p.m. in South Kingstown. The same afternoon, American Legion Post 85 in Woonsocket plans a Polka Fest from noon to 5 p.m., offering another all-ages live-music option.

Times, ticket availability and venue policies can change, so attendees should confirm details directly with organizers before traveling. The mix reflects the compact geography of Rhode Island’s cultural calendar: a weekend can move from a major Providence stage to community-scale festivals elsewhere in the state without requiring long-distance travel.
dek: Tom Papa, a new South County folk festival and a Woonsocket polka gathering anchor a varied September 11–13 events calendar.
headline: Rhode Island weekend offers comedy, folk music and polka
